purpose: Trodelvy is used to treat certain types of breast cancer (including triple-negative breast cancer and hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer) as well as a type of bladder cancer called urothelial cancer. It is typically used when other treatments have already been tried. Your doctor chose this medicine because it can specifically target cancer cells while trying to protect healthy cells as much as possible.
how_it_works: Think of this medicine as a smart guided missile. It has two parts: an antibody that acts like a homing device to find cancer cells, and a powerful chemotherapy drug attached to it. The antibody locks onto a protein found mostly on cancer cells, delivers the chemotherapy directly inside the cancer cell, and destroys it. This helps attack the cancer more precisely than traditional chemotherapy alone.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, tiredness or weakness, low blood cell counts (which can raise infection risk or cause anemia), hair loss, loss of appetite, belly pain, and rash. Diarrhea and low white blood cell counts are especially common and important to watch.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious or life-threatening diarrhea — tell your care team right away if you have loose stools so it can be treated quickly. It can significantly lower your white blood cell count, making it easier to get serious infections — watch for fever, chills, or signs of infection. It may cause severe allergic reactions during or after the infusion. It can harm an unborn baby, so use reliable birth control during treatment and for a period afterward. Always tell your doctor about all medications and supplements you take.
typical_dosing: Trodelvy is given as an IV infusion (through a vein) at a clinic or infusion center, usually once a week for two weeks in a row, followed by one week off — that three-week cycle is then repeated. The exact dose is based on your body weight. Your doctor may adjust or delay doses depending on how your body responds and any side effects you experience.
